subject: PoC operational acceptance checklist & runbook — Neurolytics
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@neurolytics.ai>, infra@neurolytics.ai
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: PoC operational acceptance checklist & runbook — Neurolytics

Hi Sarah — thanks for the demo and the honest conversation earlier. As promised, I wanted to capture the operational acceptance criteria and a proposed runbook so your team can review and confirm. I pulled together specific KPIs, owners, and a short timeline so we can convert next week’s call into an executable PoC (pilot) we can both sign off on.

High-level PoC goals (2 weeks active testing, 3 total weeks including prep & readout):
- Validate production-like inference economics and latency under your sample cohort
- Ensure quality meets your product bar for ranking + QA flows
- Confirm integration and telemetry for cost/latency/quality monitoring

Operational acceptance checklist (must-pass items):
1) Latency: p95 generation latency <= 300 ms for chat flows at typical prompt lengths (avg 150 tokens).
2) Throughput: steady-state 45–60 QPS achievable with our recommended batching; ability to burst to 120 QPS for short periods.
3) Cost: end-to-end cost/token (inference) below $0.0006/token given expected request mix.
4) Quality: human-eval pass rate >= 88% on the pilot sample (see eval rubric in Drive) and hallucination rate < 2% measured on the labeled set.
5) Stability: <1% error rate (5xx/timeout) over 24 hours of steady load during the test window.
6) Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency percentiles, and KV-cache hit metrics visible in Console.

Proposed roles & owners:
- Customer owner (Neurolytics): Sarah Lin — data/requirements, acceptance sign-off.
- Redwood Sales (owner of trial): Ben Carter — timeline, contract/kickoff.
- Redwood CS / Ops: Monica Patel — runbook execution, test harness, telemetry.
- Solutions / Integration: Lauren Bishop — model selection, prompt templates, load configuration.

Deliverables we’ll provide before active window:
- PoC scope workbook (attached) with sample prompts and labeled eval set
- Load profile CSV for your infra team to mirror (attached)
- One-page runbook with rollback and fallback model variants (Drive link)

Next steps / proposed timeline:
- Fri 5/21: confirm scope workbook and telemetry endpoints (Sarah + infra)
- Mon 5/24: environment & API keys provisioned; smoke test window (Redwood + Neurolytics)
- Tue 5/25 — Thu 6/03: active 10-business-day run window (collect logs/evals)
- Fri 6/04: readout and acceptance review

Please flag anything that’s off or additional constraints (data residency, IP restrictions, or specific SLA must-haves). If that timeline looks good I’ll send a short SOW addendum and get Monica to schedule the runbook prep call with your infra folks.

Attachments: neurolytics_poc_scope.xlsx, sample_load_profile.csv

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Lin <sarah@neurolytics.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: infra@neurolytics.ai, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PoC operational acceptance checklist & runbook — Neurolytics

Thanks Ben — this is great and captures the items we discussed. A few clarifications from infra and product: 

- For latency we typically measure end-to-end including network overhead; would p95 <= 300ms be acceptable if that excludes CDN hops? We want to be explicit about client-to-backend vs inference-only.
- For quality: our internal threshold is 90% on critical-path intents. Is there wiggle room if we hit 88–89% but show clear improvement with prompt tuning in the first 3 days?
- Data residency: we need logs retained for 90 days in the us-east-1 region. Can Redwood confirm retention and log access controls?

Also, infra asked whether the burst to 120 QPS requires additional capacity reservations or if Redwood can handle via autoscale during the pilot.

We’re comfortable with the timeline pending the above clarifications. We’ll review the workbook and aim to get you confirmation by EOD Friday.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Lin
Head of Product
Neurolytics
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@neurolytics.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-17T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PoC operational acceptance checklist & runbook — Neurolytics

Great questions — answers inline: 

- Latency definition: we will define two separate KPIs in the SOW: (A) inference-only p95 measured at the model host (target <= 250 ms), and (B) end-to-end p95 measured at your client (target <= 300 ms). We will provide both traces in Console so you can split the delta.
- Quality: we’re happy to gate acceptance at >= 90% for the critical-path intents. If initial tuning shows 88–89% on day 2 we’ll run a focused tuning sprint (Lauren + Monica) and re-evaluate; acceptance will be decided on the final readout. We’ll capture these as stretch vs must-pass in the workbook.
- Data residency: Redwood can retain telemetry logs for 90 days in us-east-1. We will provide a scoped read-only role for Neurolytics auditors. I’ll loop in Security if you want a SOC2 addendum.
- Burst capacity: for the pilot we can support autoscaling to 120 QPS without a formal reserved capacity purchase, but sustained capacity over 30 minutes will require a short commit or a burst add-on. For the run window we recommend burst-enabled autoscale; Monica will confirm the cost delta in the SOW.

Action items I’ll own this week:
- Send a short SOW addendum that formalizes the two latency KPIs, 90% critical intent threshold, and retention terms (Ben) — by Mon 5/18 EOD.
- Monica to publish the test harness steps and Console dashboard links (Monica) — by Tue 5/19.
- Lauren to share prompt-template examples and a short tuning checklist (Lauren) — by Tue 5/19.

Monica / Lauren — can you confirm you’re aligned on the owners and timelines?

Thanks — Ben
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Neurolytics PoC runbook & owner checklist

Internal note — copying the plan from the external thread and breaking into our ops checklist. This stays internal until SOW is sent.

Summary: Neurolytics wants a 10-business-day active run validating latency, throughput, cost/token, and quality. Sarah asked for 90% critical-intent acceptance and 90-day log retention. We agreed to two KPI definitions (inference-only and end-to-end).

Redwood deliverables & owners: 
- Draft SOW addendum (Ben) — includes KPI definitions, retention, and burst pricing. Target: 2027-05-18 EOD.
- Test harness + Console dashboard (Monica) — include token-level cost, p50/p95/p99, KV cache hits, and error rates. Target: 2027-05-19 EOD.
- Prompt tuning checklist + model variant plan (Lauren) — include fallback model versions, quantization profiles, and expected latency deltas. Target: 2027-05-19 EOD.
- Runbook dry-run (Monica + Lauren) — execute smoke tests on 5/24.
- Readout deck (Ben + Monica) — post-run acceptance review on 6/04.

Note on measurements & acceptance: we will gate acceptance on the labeled eval set in the workbook. Monica — please ensure the eval harness logs per-sample labels so we can compute hallucination rate and intent accuracy automatically.

Attachments for internal review: neurolytics_poc_scope.xlsx (contains eval rubric), sample_load_profile.csv

I’ll produce the SOW addendum now and request Sarah’s signature once it’s in HubSpot.

— Ben
